newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says president resigns over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says president resigns over scandal.

text.p: Japan's top brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd, said on Friday that its president Hideo Sakamaki was resigning from his post in the wake of a scandal over suspected illegal deals involving a corporate client.

Nomura said in a statement that Sakamaki's resignation is effective as of Friday and he becomes an adviser to the company. Chairman Masashi Suzuki will take on the job of president in addition to the chairmanship.

The scandal broke last week when Nomura said two of its directors made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client linked by Japanese media to a former "sokaiya" racketeer. The two directors resigned on Monday.

The case is another blot on the reputation of corporate Japan after a spate of scandals over unauthorised trading in the bond and copper markets, shady oil deals and overly cosy ties in the "iron triangle" of politics, business and bureaucracy.

Sakamaki's resignation, however, was not a big surprise to the securities industry as speculation had already been rife that such a management sacrifice was inevitable after the brokerage was hit by its second scandal in just six years.
Sakamaki's predecessor in the post stepped down over a scandal in 1991 over improper compensation of elite clients and links between Nomura affiliates and organised crime.
